message.author: me
message.excerpt: The reviewer left comments on the SDK cache PR (#226). Go through them with me.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Three threads in the review: whether the shared cache is the default with no experiment set, whether cached plans can go stale forever, and whether the byte-for-byte fixtures are worth keeping. Plus a minor note on logging fallbacks.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Shared cache by default, agreed. On staleness: what would a maximum-age check involve?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It needs service changes too, and caps cache life at that age. The service already republishes the plan on every change, so I’d skip it.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: No expiry cap then. Do we need a runbook for fixing stale entries?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Worth having. I created a task to write the SOP and will draft it after #226 merges; Priya from on-call reviews it before it goes on the wiki.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Next: are the byte-for-byte fixtures worth keeping?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Not really. They pin exact encoder bytes nothing in production depends on, and removing them lets the test-only encoder go too. The fallback-merge test leans on them, though.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Remove them. Keep fallback-merge only if it still earns its place.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Kept it, slimmed down. Three possible extra checks: a second merge reads nothing from Redis, Redis reads for a merchant’s starting plan, and one experiment decision per fee calc.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Keep the second-merge check. The merchant one sounds redundant.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It is: merchantPlan.test.ts already counts those reads. The fee-calc check folds into it and is covered too, so I dropped both.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Separate issue from the review: the SDK deletes cache entries it can’t read. Should it?

message.author: me
message.excerpt: What does the service do with those entries?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It repairs them on the next publish. I removed the SDK’s delete path and its metric.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Side note: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both carry the sub-agent rule. Remove it from CLAUDE.md?

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Should the service serve default plans from the shared cache too?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Yes. I opened PR #757 for it; review found nothing blocking. Approve?

message.excerpt: The reviewer left comments on the SDK cache PR (#226). Go through them with me.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Three threads in the review: whether the shared cache is the default with no experiment set, whether cached plans can go stale forever, and whether the byte-for-byte fixtures are worth keeping. Plus a minor note on logging fallbacks.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Shared cache by default, agreed. On staleness: what would a maximum-age check involve?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It needs service changes too, and caps cache life at that age. The service already republishes the plan on every change, so I’d skip it.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: No expiry cap then. Do we need a runbook for fixing stale entries?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Worth having. I created a task to write the SOP and will draft it after #226 merges; Priya from on-call reviews it before it goes on the wiki.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Next: are the byte-for-byte fixtures worth keeping?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Not really. They pin exact encoder bytes nothing in production depends on, and removing them lets the test-only encoder go too. The fallback-merge test leans on them, though.

message.author: me
message.excerpt: Remove them. Keep fallback-merge only if it still earns its place.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Kept it, slimmed down. Three possible extra checks: a second merge reads nothing from Redis, Redis reads for a merchant’s starting plan, and one experiment decision per fee calc.

message.excerpt: Keep the second-merge check. The merchant one sounds redundant.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It is: merchantPlan.test.ts already counts those reads. The fee-calc check folds into it and is covered too, so I dropped both.

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: Separate issue from the review: the SDK deletes cache entries it can’t read. Should it?

message.author: me
message.excerpt: What does the service do with those entries?

message.author: agent
message.excerpt: It repairs them on the next publish. I removed the SDK’s delete path and its metric.

message.excerpt: Side note: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both carry the sub-agent rule. Remove it from CLAUDE.md?
